value.name: Asha argues codicil should remain unexamined
value.description: Asha says the house should be governed by the instrument that reflects the decedent's final intent and that probing the missing codicil would introduce a criminal allegation into a stabilized probate.
evidence: house is now governed by an instrument that reflects, by every indication available to me, the actual final intent of the decedent.
To prosecute the question of how the codicil came to be missing would be to introduce a criminal allegation into a probate that has just, against considerable odds, stabilized itself.
I would prefer to leave the question available rather than to ask it.

value.name: Halloran questions who may accuse
value.description: Halloran asks who the unresolved question is being left available to, prompting Asha to identify the possible accusers.
evidence: "To the sister. To the housekeeper. To Daniel himself, eventually, if he wants to give an account of it. It is their inheritance. It is their accusation to make or to set down."

value.name: Halloran praises Asha's restraint
value.description: Halloran reflects that Asha's position is either wise or tender, signaling his uncertainty about her motives.
evidence: "That is either very wise of you," he said, "or very tender of you, and I do not yet know which."

value.name: Halloran sends Asha home
value.description: Halloran tells Asha to go home, and when she objects that it is only two in the afternoon, he insists she leave anyway and take time to be herself before tomorrow's mediation.
evidence: "Go home anyway. Or go for a walk. Or sit in a café with a book. Tomorrow you are going to spend the morning in that dining room mediating a fair-market appraisal among three people who an hour ago discovered they own a house together, and you are going to need to be a person and not a function when you do it. Go."
value.time_hint: two in the afternoon; tomorrow morning

value.name: Asha leaves
value.description: Asha complies with Halloran's instruction and departs.
